lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hey Alex, Marcus here. How's your Wednesday going?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi! Yes, now's good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Here's what I had in mind for today, but tell me if you'd rather focus on something else.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Actually, I had a question about what to eat at parties.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How are you doing, really?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Tired, but okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the walks after dinner fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days. My daughter keeps reminding me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: A short walk after dinner, even 10 minutes, really helps bring blood sugar down.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes. If I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've made up your mind.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need this for my head too, not just my body.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You feel like you have to do something.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You figured that out on your own.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good question.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you eat dinner at the same time every day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet. My family eats late, like at 9, and I'm not going to eat alone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good for you for planning ahead.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Could someone in the family walk with you?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: A short walk after dinner, even 10 minutes, really helps bring blood sugar down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday. At least I'm trying.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What feels doable for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 4 days?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, if it rains I'll walk in the hallway of my building.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Alex. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

tags.note: Checks how participant is really doing
Asks yes/no about ability to walk
Names a planning strategy that works
Commits to phone alarm as a step
Expresses own reason for change: mental health
Asks what worked on good days
Barrier: family eats late, won't eat alone
Asks what is doable next week

flags.reason: Participant voiced own reason ('I need this for my head'); coach responded with autonomy filler instead of exploring it.
Repeats unsolicited walk benefit after participant's 'I guess' and 'Maybe'; pushes advice again without permission.
Party-eating question was raised and acknowledged ('Good question') but never answered or scheduled.
Participant said 'Tired' in response to a check-in; fatigue was not explored further (not an urgent symptom as described).

score.summary: Marcus offered autonomy-supporting statements and helped Alex build a walking plan with a realistic barrier backup. However, he repeated unsolicited advice, missed Alex's change talk about mental health, and left the party-eating question unanswered.
strengths: Line 23: credited Alex's own insight ('You figured that out on your own').
Line 14 and 40 follow-up: explored Alex's planning strategy and committed days.
Line 44: asked about barriers, leading to the rain backup plan in line 45.
coaching_tips: Line 19: when Alex says 'I need this for my head,' reflect it and ask what that means to them rather than redirecting.
Line 34: avoid repeating advice after hesitant replies; ask permission first or reflect the ambivalence.
Line 17: avoid declaring 'You've made up your mind' before the participant confirms commitment; use a question instead.
Line 4 and 26: answer or schedule the party-eating question before moving on; close with a summary and next contact.
